title: Reviewer second-review and unplanned-valid decisions can dead-end or requeue items incorrectly

original_titles.title: Reviewer decision needs_second_review dead-ends the submission
No auto double review, SLA/age timers, or capacity forecast (RV-04a/03b/01a/05a, RVC-01a S2)
Review console lacks SLA timers, double review and calibration
Review workbench and disputes partial: no AI panel, ground-truth excerpt, run result or second reviewer (C-66, A-22, A-23)
Review queue: no matcher features/confidence/SLA, no automatic double review, decision possible without claim
Dispute resolution independence and participant notification unenforced
Reviewer acceptance of a never-claimed report scores nothing (manual-decision gap)
SUB-01: no filters, no reviewer reason codes, dispute window not time-bounded
Review queue lacks SLA timers and blind double review

problem: record_decision maps needs_second_review to submission status in_review but then marks the review_items row decided. The queue only selects open/claimed rows, so the second review is not created. unplanned_valid sets submission to needs_review and enqueues create_review_item, while the original review item is marked decided; repeated re-queueing can loop. Decisions can also be recorded on an open, unclaimed item if no other reviewer has claimed it.
impact: A report can disappear from the queue without a second reviewer, or cycle back to a queue with no explicit terminal decision. Manual reviewer decisions may be unauditable in terms of claim ownership and review separation.

verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Model review workflow as explicit states: open, claimed, first_decided, second_review_required, second_claimed, terminal_decided, escalated. Make allowed transitions a single tested state machine.
For needs_second_review, create a separate review assignment linked to the first decision and require a different reviewer id. Do not mark the only review item terminal before the new item exists.
For unplanned_valid, create a candidate-bug escalation record with pending/rejected/accepted status, rather than creating the same review item again.
Require the reviewer to own a current claim before decision, unless a documented organizer override is used. Store claim expiry and enforce it with DB time.
Add SLA timestamps, queue age metrics, auto-escalation and calibration reporting. Test item state after every decision, two reviewers cannot be the same person, and retries are idempotent.

acceptance_criteria: Every decision reaches one explicit terminal state or an explicit escalation state.
Second review uses a different reviewer.
Unclaimed decisions are rejected unless override is audited.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.
